image_description: The image displays the dorsal view of a crocodilian swimming in rippled water. Only the top of the head, eyes, nostrils, and a portion of the armored back are visible above the surface. The rest of the body is submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout appears relatively narrow and V-shaped, consistent with a crocodile rather than the broader U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the jawline is at or below the water level; teeth are not visible for verification.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Eyes are clearly positioned on the top of the head (dorsal), allowing the animal to see while submerged. Resolution prevents verifying slit pupils or membranes, but the positioning is correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are visible at the anterior tip of the snout, appearing as raised bumps.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the back shows a rugged, armored texture typical of crocodilians.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct ridges and bony protrusions (scutes) are visible along the spine and back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is dark grey/brown and the texture appears rough and wet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral surface (belly) is completely submerged and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are submerged and not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the cropped image.

alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the 'African crocodile' class. All testable checkpoints regarding the head shape, eye position, nostril placement, and dorsal armor texture are present and accurate. Several checkpoints were untestable due to the subject being partially submerged (teeth, belly, limbs, tail), but no contradictions were found in the visible anatomy. The V-shaped snout correctly distinguishes it from an alligator.
artifact_reasoning: No AI-generation artifacts detected. The water ripples interact naturally with the subject's body, showing appropriate displacement and refraction. Textures on the skin are consistent and realistic. There is no evidence of melting, structural collapse, or boundary bleeding.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
